Pricing._comment: Public list prices for the ids the per-token API providers default to (#682). Every entry is copied from the vendor page in `_source` on `EffectiveDate`; nothing here is a guess. Ids served over a subscription transport (Copilot, Claude CLI, Codex) have no per-token price to cite and are deliberately absent. Schema and citation list: docs/features/public-pricing-catalog.md.

SubAgentIntelligence._comment: Map tiers 0-6 to ordered model-id fallback arrays. This is NOT only the tier ladder: SubAgentModelResolver derives the sanctioned model-override allow-list (IsKnownModel) AND the id menu the Agent tool descriptor advertises from exactly these values. An empty ladder therefore also empties the allow-list, so every `model` override the parent LLM sends is rejected as 'unknown' — including real, in-catalog ids (gpt-5.6-luna, the model actually running, was rejected in production) — and the descriptor lists no ids, so the parent invents them ('gpt-5', 'gpt-5.2', 'sonnet'). A tier mapped to [] is now reported as MISCONFIGURED by SubAgentIntelligenceOptions.Load and dropped, so the 'Tiers is empty' diagnostic can actually fire. Every tier below is pinned to the model in use today (gpt-5.6-luna), so populating the ladder changes no routing and no spend; a deployment override (e.g. appsettings.Development.json) or a one-line edit here is all it takes to spread the tiers across models.
SubAgentIntelligence._tier_mapping_comment: OWNER-APPROVED MAPPING (separately revertable): tier 1 mechanical fan-out stays on gpt-5.6-luna, tier 3 -> gpt-5.6-terra, tier 5 -> gpt-5.6-sol. Tiers 0/2/4/6 are NOT part of that approval and remain pinned to the model in use today (gpt-5.6-luna); note this leaves tiers 4 and 6 CHEAPER than tier 5, so a climb from 4 or 6 lands on luna while 5 lands on sol. That inversion is an open owner decision, not an oversight — map 4 and 6 deliberately to close it.

AgentCollaboration._comment: Hierarchy-wide agent collaboration (#244). With Enabled omitted (as here) the chat mode decides: the Workspace Agent runs WITH collaboration — peer messaging, a hierarchy roster, and transcript reads bounded by TranscriptVisibility (Ancestors | Open) — while Workflow Author and the ordinary modes keep the pre-#244 tool surface and nesting limits. Add "Enabled": true or false to override every mode in that direction. The limits below apply wherever collaboration is on; MaxDelegationDepth counts ordinary spawn hops from the root (0), and a workflow controller is a free hop.

AzureAd._comment: Entra app registration for interactive sign-in (P1 #301). ClientId EMPTY here on purpose: with no client id no JWT bearer handler is registered at all, the SPA renders without a sign-in gate, and the whole identity pipeline is inert. That is the state every development machine and every existing test runs in. TenantId 'organizations' admits any work or school directory but not personal Microsoft accounts; which tenant a user belongs to is discovered from their token's tid and resolved against the tenants table, never pinned here.

Identity._comment: Enforce is GLOBAL - one process-wide flag, not per tenant (this supersedes the per-tenant flag of #237). False means an unauthenticated /api request resolves to a development principal rather than being refused, which is what keeps every current call path working. Flipping it to true refuses anonymous /api requests for EVERYONE in this process. The operator secret guarding POST /api/admin/tenants is deliberately NOT here: it is read from the LMSTREAMING_IDENTITY_OPERATOR_SECRET environment variable, and while it is unset that route answers 503 rather than succeeding.

Audit._comment: IncludeUpn records the presented preferred_username on a REJECTED sign-in. Off by default: a rejected sign-in is exactly the case where that identifier belongs to someone who is by definition not our user.

M365._comment: EmailMcpServer Entra app (mcqdb tenant). Confidential web client; ClientSecret MUST come from env (Auth__M365__ClientSecret) — NEVER commit it. Kept in base settings (not just Development) so M365 auth + scopes apply in Production too. Callback at /auth/m365/callback.
